advances: Failure of a prescribed unique largest-fiber centroid. Other marks remain available, including within the central fiber.
author: PK-research-agent
proof: Apply the actual cube-radius construction in pk-w36-line-actual-cube-radius-truncation. Each off-zero integer fiber is $aT_d$ with volume $a^d|T_d|$, while the central fiber has volume $|T_d|$ and centroid $g=(1,\ldots,1)/(d+1)$ by barycentric permutation symmetry. In every off-zero fiber $x_1\le a$, with equality only at $ae_1$, so the closed cap contributes zero $d$-volume there. In $T_d$, the cap is $ae_1+(1-a)T_d$ and has volume $(1-a)^d|T_d|=\gamma_d|T_d|$. Division by the total mass proves the strict bound under the stated inequality. In the concrete case $1+(3^6-1)/9=737/9>64$, and $4/737<1/144$ since $576<737$.
statement: For integers $n,d\ge1$, let $T_d=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:x_i\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i\le1\}$ and let $C$ have fibers $[1-(1-a)\|z\|_\infty]T_d$ over $z\in[-1,1]^n$, with $a=1/(d+1)$. The central integer fiber $T_d$ has the unique largest volume. At its centroid $(0,g)$ the cap $x_1\ge1/(d+1)$ has raw mixed mass $\gamma_d|T_d|$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and the total mixed mass is $|T_d|[1+(3^n-1)/(d+1)^d]$. Thus this centroid has normalized mixed depth strictly below $\gamma_d/2^n$ whenever $1+(3^n-1)/(d+1)^d>2^n$. At $n=6,d=2$ the bracket is $737/9$ and the cap fraction is $4/737<1/144$.
title: The unique peak centroid fails in the symmetric cube-radius family
